gaps.text: Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Low-level fusion: synchronised NIR reflection and Raman spectra merged into one augmented matrix, as in the published feed-frame work. Both probes must sample the same powder spot, and data must be normalised to a common time step with block scaling so neither method dominates. Each method keeps its own calibration, and the fused model must beat the best single method on independent runs or the extra instrument is dropped.)

items.finding: Combining near-infrared and Raman spectroscopy via low-level data fusion can improve step-change sensitivity and reduce root mean squared error when predicting certain blend potency levels, though noisy near-infrared spectra may provide no added benefit for lower concentration ranges.
items.how_it_applies: When testing the combined fiber probe setup in the feed frame, evaluate whether low-level data fusion improves the model for the target API concentration range or if the individual method performs adequately.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The published findings are based on a specific five-component platform formulation and specific concentration ranges, so transfer to the customer's powder blend and equipment scale must be verified experimentally.

citation.quote: For model development and validation, low-level data fusion was explored through concatenation of preprocessed NIR and Raman spectra. Mid-level data fusion was also evaluated, based on extracted features of the preprocessed data.
